evidence_class: Mocked Redis (fakeredis), a fake clock and a fake Pod source that emits list, watch, expired cursor, connection reset and deletion events; no Kubernetes API, node autoscaler or EC2 call was made.
interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.kubernetes.watch: OWNER_LABEL and EXECUTION_LABEL, owner_for(slug) as the plan independent owner value, labels(owner, execution_id), PodSource with list_pods, watch_pods, read_pod and delete_pod under a uid precondition
PodView keys observed Pods by uid and relists on an expired cursor, a connection error or a timeout

Reconciler.plan classifies managed orphan, missing pod, foreign, ambiguous, terminating and superseded Pods; a live Pod of a superseded generation of a seat is kept and counted, never deleted; cleanup is a constructor switch independent of matching

Controller(pods=PodView, orphan_cleanup=bool): acquire reconciles after operation recovery and before admission opens; reconcile() plans from the current kubernetes execution occupants, treats every other recorded execution as superseded, deletes an orphan only when a fresh read still equals the observed Pod and the lease and grant still hold, and writes the class counts only after a final lease check
Controller.controller_orphans_by_class() reads the latest counts from the per swarm controller-orphans hash

supported_versions.redis: Hashes only; the counts hash is observational
supported_versions.kubernetes: Any API that supports label selector list, resource version watch with 410 expiry and delete preconditions on uid; no client is wired yet
supported_versions.compatibility: A Controller without a Pod view reconciles nothing and writes no counts key: the SV2-CTL-01 to 03 controller and admission tests pass unchanged, and a test asserts no controller-orphans key exists without a view; the local herdr path is unchanged

authority: Every reconcile and every delete re-checks the scoped controller grant and the lease through the controller authority check. The owner label value derives from the swarm slug, never from a Pod name or display label. A Pod lacking the owner label is never listed; a Pod with another owner, an empty execution id or a twin for one execution is quarantined, never deleted. Case B revokes the grant mid run: reconcile refuses with the exact grant error and deletes nothing.

states.observed: Cases A, B and C each passed twice from independent fake Redis servers and Pod sources with identical outputs. Controller, watch and size limit tests passed, 87 in total.
states.accepted: A restarted controller matches the existing managed Pod, deletes only the managed orphan and launches nothing; unlabelled lookalikes are never listed, foreign owners and ambiguous Pods leave protected state unchanged; an expired cursor or a connection reset relists, and a delayed deletion of an old incarnation leaves the newer Pod matched.
states.committed: Code and fixture inputs are at tested_commit.
states.externally_verified: None: no Kubernetes Pod source is wired and no live G3 deployment was exercised.

rollback_rehearsal.action: Construct the controller with orphan_cleanup False: status matching and missing pod detection continue while no Pod is deleted. The runtime package that constructs the controller binds this switch from its GitOps configuration; until then the switch is the constructor argument.
rollback_rehearsal.authoritative_objects: The execution journal (executions hash, controller intents, runtime operations) and the Kubernetes Pods themselves; the controller-orphans counts hash is observational and safe to discard.
rollback_rehearsal.proof: Case C restarts a controller with cleanup disabled over the same store after a managed orphan appears: the orphan survives, the newer incarnation stays matched and no launch happens.

remaining_limitations: No Pod creation path exists yet; the Kubernetes runtime package must label every Pod it creates with labels(owner_for(slug), execution_id), otherwise its Pods are never listed and cannot be matched or cleaned. Tracked by https://github.com/the-cloud-clockwork/agentihooks/issues/2078; issue 2050 stays open until it closes.
No Kubernetes API Pod source exists yet; it must implement PodSource over label selector list, watch with 410 expiry and delete with a uid precondition.

The lease check and the Pod delete are not one transaction: a controller paused after its final lease check can still issue one delete, as the takeover test shows. The PodSource contract requires a uid precondition, which limits that delete to the exact orphan observed, and execution ids are fresh per attempt, so a new leader never adopts that Pod; the stale controller then refuses to write counts.
Missing pod executions are reported, not relaunched; relaunch stays with the tick and admission path.
A live Pod of a superseded generation is kept and counted as superseded; no path drains or deletes it yet, which belongs to the drain and outcome packages.
Quarantined Pods are counted and returned on the plan but not persisted for operator review.
controller_orphans_by_class is a Redis hash read through a method; no telemetry exporter emits it yet.
Mutation qualification is pending the pull request CI run.
